title: Back to the Future: Great Scott!
description: Clock towers, flux capacitors, and teenage destiny—time-travel depths.

questions.question: Real DeLorean speedometers stopped at 85 mph, so the movie car needed a custom one. What speed sends Doc's DeLorean through time?
questions.hint: Great Scott! This is the magic number
questions.explanation: Bob Gale wanted a speed nobody would hit by accident and everybody would remember: "88 just had the right ring to it." The movie car got a digital readout to show it off.

questions.question: Hitting 88 mph, the DeLorean's flux capacitor needs how much power?
questions.explanation: Doc says "jigowatts" because an engineer the writers consulted pronounced it that way, and Bob Gale spelled it "jigowatt" in the script. In 1955, only a lightning bolt packs that punch.

questions.question: Sent back by 1.21 gigawatts, Marty meets the bully who torments his father at Hill Valley High—who?
questions.hint: Make like a tree and get outta here!
questions.explanation: Zemeckis and Gale named Biff after Universal exec Ned Tanen, who blew up at them over an earlier script. Biff's comeuppance in 1955: a crash into a manure truck.

questions.question: After confronting Biff Tannen, what song does Marty sing lead on at the Enchantment Under the Sea dance?
questions.hint: Chuck Berry song that's a little before their time
questions.explanation: Marvin Berry phones his cousin Chuck: "You know that new sound you're looking for? Well, listen to this!" Marty's verdict on the stunned crowd: "Your kids are gonna love it."

questions.question: Michael J. Fox lip-synced "Johnny B. Goode," but he wasn't the first Marty. Which actor filmed the role for weeks before being replaced?
questions.hint: He later played Lance in Pulp Fiction
questions.explanation: About five weeks in, Zemeckis felt the comedy wasn't landing and recast in January 1985. Fox then shot Family Ties by day and Hill Valley by night, often until 2 a.m.
